chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musli, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman, who said:

When Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) arrived in Kufah during the time of Abi al-Abbas, he came on his mount wearing his traveling clothes until he stopped on the bridge of Kufah. Then he said to his servant, 'Give me water.' So he took a jug from the water-seller, scooped water for him with it, and gave it to him. He drank, and the water flowed from the corners of his mouth, onto his beard, and onto his clothes. Then he asked for more, and he gave him more. He praised Allah and said: 'What a great blessing is this river of water! Verily, every day seven drops fall into it from Paradise. If people knew the blessing in it, they would pitch their tents on its banks. If it were not for what enters it from the sinners, no one with an ailment would immerse himself in it without being cured.'

key_terms.الْكَوفَة: Kufah, a major city in Iraq

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical blessings of the Euphrates River according to Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.)?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the Euphrates (Al-Furat) as a sacred site for ziyarat, emphasizing its unique spiritual status through the Imam’s declaration that seven drops of Paradise’s water fall into it daily. The text underscores the river's dual nature: it possesses inherent healing properties for the physically afflicted, yet its purity can be affected by the impurities of sinners, reflecting the Shia concept of the interplay between divine blessing and human conduct. This tradition serves to encourage pilgrims to drink from and perform ghusl in the river, viewing it as a conduit of barakah during the Abbasid era.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 9. Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from Ḥasan ibn Sa’īd, from ‘Ali ibn Ḥakam, from Rabī’ ibn Muḥammad Al-Musli, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Sulaymān, who said:

When Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) came to Kūfah during the time of Abil ‘Abbās, he was on his mount and was wearing his traveling attire. He stopped on the bridge of Kūfah and asked his servant to give him some water. So the servant took a jug and filled it (from the Euphrates River) and gave it to the Imam (a.s.). The Imam (a.s.) started drinking, and (as he was drinking) the water spilled from the two corners of his mouth onto his beard and onto his clothes. Then the Imam (a.s.) asked for some more water. The servant refilled the jug and gave it to the Imam (a.s.). After the Imam (a.s.) drank the water, he praised Allāh and said: What a blessed river this river is! Verily every day seven drops of water fall from Paradise into it. If people knew of the blessings of this river, they would build their tents on its shores. Verily if it was not for that which enters this river from the sinners, no ill person would submerge himself in it without being cured.
